descriptionChirho: Feminine noun meaning 'watch', a division of the night used for military guard duty and as a measure of nighttime hours. The Israelite night was divided into three watches. Attested in Exod 14:24 and 1 Sam 11:11 (בְּאַשְׁמֹרֶת הַבֹּקֶר 'in the morning watch'), Judg 7:19 (רֹאשׁ הָאַשְׁמֹרֶת הַתִּיכוֹנָה 'the beginning of the middle watch'), Ps 63:6 (בְּאַשְׁמֻרוֹת 'in the night watches' of meditation), Ps 90:4 (a thousand years like a watch in the night), Ps 119:148 (eyes anticipating the night watches), Lam 2:19 (crying out at the head of every watch). All auto-split clusters represent the same noun in singular and plural forms with various prepositions and the article. Glosses confirm: arb هزيع 'night watch', deu Nachtwache, fra veille, hin पहर, kor 야경/새벽경비, spa vigilia/guardia.
